message:
security: opencode's extension signing key is not ours to commit

opencode/ext-key.pem is an RSA private key - the signing key for the browser
extension, generated on this machine. It reached a commit because ~/.config/
opencode is now a symlink into this repo and `git add -A` swept it up with
opencode's own edits.

It never left the machine: the commit holding it was not pushed, and
raw.githubusercontent still answers 404 for it. Untracked and ignored here;
the commit that introduced it is rewritten separately.

A scan of all 1836 tracked files finds no other key material - the remaining
matches are design tokens (tokens.css, tokens.scss), a Python attribute called
self.password, and a test fixture that spells out sk-must-not-reach-codex.

message:
fix: fish -c reported failure for work it had just done

`fish -c 'set -q X; or set -Ux X v'` sets the variable and then exits 1: fish
reports the status of the `set -q` that opened the line, not of the branch that
actually ran. So `fish-universals` was marked FAILED on every fresh install
while having correctly set every variable, and `fish-plugins` next to it hit
the same shape.

Measured in a container: the `or` form exits 1 with AAA=7 already set; `if not
set -q BBB; set -Ux BBB 8; end` exits 0 with BBB=8, and exits 0 again when BBB
is already there. All five lines use the if form now.

message:
fix: glass stopped working because a tag outlived the state that set it

`hl.window_rule({ match = { fullscreen = true }, tag = "+hyprglass_disabled" })`
looked like a free optimisation - a fullscreen window has no visible edge, so
why spend the GPU. But a tag is not a state: the window goes fullscreen once,
picks the tag up, leaves fullscreen, and keeps it forever.

So the glass degraded quietly, window by window, as things were fullscreened
over a session. Caught on this machine with hyprctl:

  kitty          fullscreen=0  tags=['hyprglass_disabled*', 'hyprglass_enabled*']
  google-chrome  fullscreen=0  tags=['hyprglass_disabled*']

Neither was fullscreen; chrome had been, for one video. Nothing else in the
repo tags chrome disabled - the only other disable rule is mpv|vlc|imv.

The rule is gone, with a comment saying why it must not come back. Verified: a
newly mapped kitty now carries hyprglass_enabled and nothing else. Windows that
were already poisoned keep the tag until they are re-mapped - Hyprland does not
drop a rule-derived tag on reload - so they need reopening once.

message:
security: root must not put a user-writable path on the system PATH

The wallust fallback linked /usr/local/bin/wallust at ~/.local/bin/wallust.
Anything able to write that file - any process running as the user - would
then decide what runs when root, or any other user, types `wallust`. A local
privilege escalation in exchange for saving one copy.

It installs a root-owned copy instead, with `install -m 0755 -o root -g root`
so the owner and mode are set as the file appears rather than after. A test
fails on any future `sudo ln ... $HOME ...`.
